hypotheses.title: Uninitialized-variable CFG analysis clones the full per-local state map at every basic block (O(blocks x locals))
hypotheses.issue: Stage 8 uninitialized-variable analysis (semantics/internal/cfg/uninitialized_var_analyzer.go) keeps a map[SymbolRef]bool of variable init state and copies it at every basic block. analyzeNode calls markInitialized for every BLangVariableDef with an initializer, so every ordinary local (`int v = expr;`) is tracked, although such a variable can never be reported as uninitialized; only declarations without initializer (`int x;`) can. Therefore the state holds every local declared so far, and per block: mergePredecessors clones the first predecessor's exit state, mergeStates allocates two fresh maps (allVars + result) per extra predecessor, and analyze clones the entry state again before analyzeBlock; both entry (never read) and exit states for all blocks are retained in a map[int]*blockState until the function is done. clone uses an un-presized map so maps.Copy rehashes repeatedly. Cost is O(blocks x locals) time and memory: long functions with many locals and branches spend almost all compile time here (maps.Copy ~45% CPU, maps.Copy+mergeStates ~93% of bytes allocated on the reproducer).

reproducer.generator:
"""Generate a single long function with many local variables and many basic blocks.

No type narrowing, no else-less ifs: each step declares an initialized int local and
branches on it with an if/else, so the CFG has O(n) blocks and O(n) tracked locals.
"""
import sys

n = int(sys.argv[1])
out = ["import ballerina/io;", "",
       "function step(int i) returns int {", "    return i % 7;", "}", "",
       "function run() returns int {", "    int acc = 0;"]
for i in range(n):
    out.append(f"    int v{i} = step({i});")
    out.append(f"    if v{i} > 3 {{ acc += v{i}; }} else {{ acc -= 1; }}")
out += ["    return acc;", "}", "", "public function main() {", "    io:println(run());", "}"]
print("\n".join(out))
reproducer.command: python3 gen_uninit.py 2000 > uninit_vars.bal; hyperfine -w 1 -r 5 'bal run uninit_vars.bal'; /usr/bin/time -f 'wall %e s maxrss %M KB' bal run --stats uninit_vars.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: Track only variables declared without an initializer: on a VariableDef with an initializer, set it true only if it is already tracked (e.g. foreach implicit vars) instead of inserting it. Pitfall: mergeStates treats an empty state as an 'unvisited block' and returns the other side; with fewer tracked vars, empty maps become common, so a separate hasVars flag (set by every mark*, copied by clone, true on merge results) replaces the len()==0 check to keep the exact old semantics. Also: dropped the never-read entry state and its extra clone (analyze passes the merged state straight to analyzeBlock), replaced map[int]*blockState with a []*varInitState of exit states, pre-sized clone/merge maps, and removed the allVars temporary map in mergeStates (iterate s1, then add s2-only keys as false). Diagnostics are unchanged because a reference to an initialized-declared var cannot be reached on a path skipping its declaration (lexical scoping; back edges are ignored). make test passes. A bitset indexed by local or copy-on-write states would further reduce cost for code with many uninitialized declarations.

notes: Exploration also noted (unmeasured) a possible O(N^2) in semantics/internal/types/type_resolver_narrowing.go: lookupBindingInner walks the whole narrowing binding chain for every non-narrowed variable reference, and commonAncestor/chainDepth walks both chains fully on each mergeChains call; candidate for a future hunt.
